items.title: Fake Chrome Update Pop-Ups Are Spreading Malware
items.summary: Security writers are warning about fake browser-update pop-ups: a notice claiming your browser needs a "critical update." Clicking it installs malware, not an update. Real updates come from the browser's own menu — never from a website pop-up. If you see one, close the tab without clicking, then update properly: in Chrome, click the three dots, choose **Help → About Google Chrome**, and let it update itself. Then check your extensions and remove anything you don't recognize.

items.title: 300+ malicious Chrome extensions caught leaking browser data — audit yours in Chrome's Extensions manager
items.summary: Security researchers found more than 300 malicious Chrome extensions collecting browsing history or stealing user information. Open Chrome, click the three dots, choose **Extensions → Manage Extensions**, and remove anything you don't recognize or no longer use.

items.title: Audit your Chrome extensions in two minutes — Manage Extensions finds the fakes
items.summary: In Chrome, click the three dots, choose **Extensions → Manage Extensions**, and turn off anything you don't recognize or no longer use — one at a time, so you'll know what changed. Real updates come from the browser's own menu, never from a website pop-up.

items.title: Windows 10 Support Ends October 14 — Check Your PC This Week
items.summary: Windows 10 support ends **October 14, 2026** — six weeks from today. After that date Microsoft stops releasing security updates for Windows 10, so newly discovered vulnerabilities won't be patched on your PC. Check which version you have now: press **Start**, type **About your PC

items.title: Scammers Are Using AI to Impersonate Charities
items.summary: Scammers are using artificial intelligence to make charity appeals sound personal and urgent. A message may use a familiar organization’s name, a copied logo, or a convincing voice recording, then ask for gift cards, cryptocurrency, or a wire transfer. Before giving, stop and visit the organization’s official website by typing its address yourself. Never use payment instructions from an unexpected message. The Federal Trade Commission says pressure to pay immediately is a major warning sign.

items.title: Chrome security update helps block dangerous websites — update Chrome at `chrome://settings/help`
items.summary: Google's Chrome release blog reports a new desktop security update. Open Chrome, select the three dots in the upper-right corner, choose **Help → About Google Chrome**, and let it update. Restart Chrome when it asks.

items.title: Apple Security Releases help protect your iPhone — install the latest iPhone update from Settings
items.summary: Apple's Security Releases page lists the latest protection for iPhones. On your iPhone, open **Settings → General → Software Update** and install the latest update. Leave the phone connected to power while it finishes.

items.title: Genetic Testing Data Breach Exposes 2.8 Million People — Your DNA Data May Be at Risk
items.summary: Big news if you or anyone in your family ever had a DNA test. Baylor Genetics — a company that runs genetic tests for cancer risk, pregnancy screening, and rare diseases — just confirmed hackers stole personal information of 2.8 million people. We are talking names, Social Security numbers, medical diagnoses, and your actual genetic test results (source: KCRA/Hearst TV, Aug 28). If that sounds like you, check baylorgenetics.com/securityupdate right now to see if you were affected. Then place a free credit freeze at all three credit bureaus — Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. Federal law makes credit freezes free, and it takes about five minutes per bureau.

items.title: Google Gemini inside Google Forms creates quizzes from your notes free — try it at forms.google.com
items.summary: Open Google Forms at forms.google.com, click the Gemini sparkle icon, type your topic or upload a PDF, and it builds a complete quiz with questions and answer choices automatically.

items.title: Clipchamp is the free video editor built into Windows 11 — edit family clips and save them without a watermark
items.summary: Press Start and type Clipchamp, open it, drag your videos onto the timeline, trim and arrange them, and export — built into Windows 11, completely free with no watermarks.

items.title: Windows Update Is Breaking Printers and PDFs — Here's What to Do
items.summary: Microsoft's latest Windows update is breaking printers and PDF saving across the country. Programs crash when you try to print or create a PDF. Here is what to do right now: open Settings, go to Windows Update, and click "Pause updates" for 7 days. If your printer already stopped working, try printing from a web browser instead. This is a Microsoft mistake, not a printer problem. They are working on a fix. Bring it by the shop if you need help — free diagnosis, no pressure. (Sources: PCWorld, BleepingComputer — August 25-26, 2026)

items.title: CISA says hackers are already using six new flaws — update your computer tonight and tell your IT department if you use Citrix at work
items.summary: The government's cybersecurity agency (CISA) added six newly exploited vulnerabilities to its catalog on August 26 — including a Citrix flaw that lets hackers break into remote access systems without a password. If your company uses Citrix for remote work, tell your IT department to patch it tonight. On your own computer, press Start, type "check for updates," open Windows Update, and install whatever is available. It takes two minutes.
